SCORE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_FINE_MARGIN | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_FINE_MARGIN | IN_SCOPE | Training-only directed transitions are counted and retained as weighted outgoing edges; hyperbolic prediction error scales fine-level geodesic assignment distances and trains the transition map, so both signals affect the computation. Behaviour-off, Euclidean and both-on switches are not specified as operational code switches.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_FINE_MARGIN | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_FINE_MARGIN | Multiplying every code distance for item i by the same positive factor leaves its hard argmin unchanged; only the soft assignments/gradients can change, and those may not affect exported SIDs reliably.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_FINE_MARGIN | For distances (1, 4) and any positive factor a, argmin(a·1,a·4)=argmin(1,4); hard SID assignment does not change.
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_FINE_MARGIN | Behavior evidence is well-supported by measured train-only entropy stratification and transition coverage (E5, E10). Geometry is genuinely computed but the proposal does not establish why this multiplicative scaling adds value over a matched Euclidean computation; moreover, the positive item-wide scalar cancels from hard nearest-code assignment. The downstream gradient path is plausible but lacks a demonstrated link to useful Stage3 predictions. The bundle proposes a matched Euclidean control but does not specify the three operational switches or establish novelty: prior-work search is NOT_CHECKED (E15). Implementability is uncertain because numerical safeguards for maps and the median fallback are partial, and the interaction of the shared scale with logits/gradient normalization needs a bounded implementation check. UNKNOWN novelty could be resolved by a bounded comparison with cited work and the existing mechanism ledger; no ablation, sweep or repeat is implied.

SCORE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL | IN_SCOPE | Training-only outgoing-transition profiles define branches, and branch-specific hyperbolic Fréchet anchors/log residuals determine fine quantizer inputs and updates. The required behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches are not specified.
EVIDENCE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL | The specification mixes a tangent residual \(u_i=\log_a(r_i)\) with a baseline codebook “mapped into the anchor’s tangent space” without defining the map/transport needed to put codewords and residuals in compatible coordinates.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL | If \(u_i\in T_a\mathcal B\) but \(c_k\in T_0\mathcal B\), then \(\|u_i-c_k\|\) is not a defined intrinsic comparison absent a specified transport; subtracting \(c_k\) at \(a\) is coordinate-dependent.
RATIONALE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FRECHET_RESIDUAL | Measured train branching and coverage support the behaviour premise (E10–E11), and the proposal explicitly uses curved log/exp maps and Fréchet averaging (E12–E14). Curvature could matter for branch-specific anchors, but no matched-control argument establishes necessity. The assignment-to-recommendation chain is plausible, not diagnostic-specific. The evidence bundle does not provide a prior-art audit or operational switches; novelty is UNKNOWN and would need a bounded comparison against the ledger and cited mechanisms. The coordinate mismatch and changing residual-dependent anchors make implementation risk substantial; clarify tangent transport and ensure anchors are computed from available residuals without an unspecified redesign.

SCORE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE | IN_SCOPE | Training-only directed, popularity-adjusted transitions form a successor embedding mean; a log-map tangent vector is added before fine-level hyperbolic assignment. Behaviour and geometry jointly affect the assignment input. Operational behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches are not fully specified in the proposal text.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14 E15
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE | The tangent vector is based at \(h_i\), while the assignment adds it to residual \(r_{i,\ell}\) at base point \(q_{i,\ell}\); these tangent spaces differ, and no parallel transport is specified.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE | On a curved manifold, \(t_i\in T_{h_i}\mathcal B\) cannot generally be added to \(r_{i,\ell}\in T_{q_{i,\ell}}\mathcal B\); even if \(h_i\ne q_{i,\ell}\), the vectors have no common tangent space without transport.
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE | The measured transition entropy and coverage support a plausible training-only signal (E5, E10), and the bundle describes curved operations and matched Euclidean controls (E12–E15). However, curvature’s added necessity is not argued against the matched control, and this is close to the already measured tangent-successor-residual family (E6–E7), so novelty is UNKNOWN pending a bounded ledger comparison. The proposed assignment steering could change fine tokens and prefix predictability, but base-point inconsistency is a blocking specification risk. Falsifiability is limited because the text does not specify three matched switches or a failure criterion.

SCORE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_GEODESIC | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_GEODESIC | IN_SCOPE | Training-only successor distributions weight a geodesic separation loss on fine quantized representations, coupling behaviour and curvature in the training objective. The proposal specifies a Euclidean control but not operational behaviour-off/geometry-off/both-on code switches.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_GEODESIC | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_MARGIN_GEODESIC | The hinge penalty is zero for pairs already at or beyond the batch median positive distance, so the loss may act only on a narrow, unstable subset while spending capacity separating pairs rather than improving useful next-item discrimination.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_GEODESIC | For a pair with \(d(z_i,z_j)\ge\rho\), \(\max(0,\rho-d)^2=0\); its successor divergence \(b_{ij}\) then contributes no gradient, however behaviorally distinct the pair is.
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_GEODESIC | Train-only successor entropy and edge coverage support the behavior premise (E5, E10). Geodesic distance is an explicit curved operation, but the proposal gives no argument that the geodesic margin does something its matched Euclidean counterpart cannot; the bundle’s geometry sanity check does not establish necessity (E16). A path from pair separation to fine assignments and recommendation is plausible. The proposal has a margin and pairwise controls in the bundle, but does not define all three operational switches or a falsifier. Pairwise minibatch computation is implementable, though pair coverage and median-scale stability are risks. Novelty is UNKNOWN because no traceable prior-art comparison is supplied; a bounded ledger/literature check would resolve it.

SCORE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE__ideation_3 | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE__ideation_3 | OUT_OF_SCOPE | The behavior signal and curved exp-map assignment are specified, but the behavior tangent \(u_i\), based at the item embedding \(x_i\), is applied to each residual representation \(x_i^\ell\) without a defined transport between base points. The required matched switches are also not operationally specified.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE__ideation_3 | E1 E2 E3 E5 E6 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14 E15
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE__ideation_3 | The proposed popularity-adjusted barycenter may not lie inside the Poincaré ball, and the tangent step is applied at residual base points despite being computed at the item embedding base point.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE__ideation_3 | If a weighted Euclidean sum of ball points has norm at least \(1/\sqrt c\), it is outside the ball and \(\log_{x_i}\) is undefined; separately, \(u_i\in T_{x_i}\) cannot be added directly at \(x_i^\ell\ne x_i\).
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_TANGENT_FINE__ideation_3 | Training-only popularity-adjusted transitions have measured entropy and coverage evidence (E5, E10). Hyperbolic exp/log operations are explicit, but their necessity versus the matched Euclidean version is not established. The bundle’s earlier tangent-successor mechanism has similar measured behavior and geometry (E6), making this a near-repeat absent a computational distinction that is demonstrated; novelty is UNKNOWN pending bounded ledger review. The intended assignment effect is plausible, but the undefined barycenter/domain guards and tangent-space mismatch undermine implementability. The bundle’s proposal does not state three operational switches or a clear falsifier.

SCORE: TRANSITION_CURVATURE_MARGIN | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: TRANSITION_CURVATURE_MARGIN | OUT_OF_SCOPE | The training-only successor-overlap signal weights a curved fine-residual separation loss, but the geometry is applied to \(\exp_0^{-1}(r_i^\ell)\) as written; this is dimensionally/manifold-wise inconsistent if \(r_i^\ell\) is already a Poincaré point. The three switches are described in the bundle but not fully specified in the supplied proposal.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_CURVATURE_MARGIN | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E12 E13 E14 E15
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_CURVATURE_MARGIN | The displayed residual mapping uses \(\exp_0^{-1}\), the inverse exponential map, as if it were the exponential map; if \(r_i^\ell\) is a tangent residual, this is undefined, and if it is a ball point, the resulting coordinate is not the claimed curved residual representation.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_CURVATURE_MARGIN | For a tangent vector \(v\), \(\exp_0^{-1}(v)\) is not defined as the Poincaré logarithm’s input unless \(v\) is first mapped to a ball point; for a ball point \(x\), \(\log_0(x)\), not \(\exp_0^{-1}(x)\) as written, is the specified operation.
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_CURVATURE_MARGIN | Train-only successor profiles and measured transition statistics make the behavior premise plausible (E5, E10). The geometric margin is explicit, but its stated residual coordinate is inconsistent and the matched Euclidean control is not enough to argue geometric necessity. The loss could alter fine codes, yet the direct effect on Stage3 behavior is only plausible. The evidence bundle specifies a Euclidean control and sanity check (E14–E16), but the provided proposal lacks all operational switches and a failure criterion. The proposal’s novelty relative to prior mechanisms is UNKNOWN; bounded ledger comparison would resolve it. The coordinate error requires a bounded implementation correction before the mechanism is safely implementable.

SCORE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_RESIDUAL | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=1 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=2 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=1 | exploration_value=1
SCOPE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_RESIDUAL | OUT_OF_SCOPE | Although it names directed training transitions and Poincaré operations, the behavior-dependent term is a target loss whose coefficient \(\alpha_i\) is a positive scalar for each item and does not make the core quantization assignment behavior-dependent; the evidence bundle’s behavior-dependency sanity check reports that a positive row scalar leaves the relevant computation unchanged. The required switches are present in the bundle’s proposed checks but not specified as complete executable controls here.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_RESIDUAL | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_RESIDUAL | The behavior target \(b_i\) is a successor barycenter, but the loss compares the selected-code tangent vector with the barycenter tangent vector in coordinates whose base point and scaling are not established as compatible; the behavior term may also not alter the assignment.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_RESIDUAL | The behavior-off switch sets \(\alpha_i=0\); if all items have zero outgoing support, every \(\alpha_i=0\), so behavior contributes no gradient and the stated mechanism reduces exactly to the baseline.
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_GEODESIC_RESIDUAL | Measured transition coverage and entropy support train-only behavioral structure (E5, E10), but the geometry evidence bundle explicitly flags behavior dependency as failed (E16). The assignment itself uses ordinary nearest-code selection and the behavior term is an auxiliary target, so coupling is not demonstrated. The construction also mixes tangent coordinates without fully specified compatible bases, making implementation incomplete. A proposed Euclidean control exists in the bundle, but three correct switches and a falsifier are not fully specified. This repeats the broader successor-residual-target family, and the bundle’s negative result in a related family (E16) reduces exploration value. Novelty is UNKNOWN without a bounded ledger check.

SCORE: BRANCH_RADIAL_FINE_CODES | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=1 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=2 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: BRANCH_RADIAL_FINE_CODES | OUT_OF_SCOPE | The behavior entropy changes a radial prototype displacement, but the proposed “geometry-off” counterpart is an Euclidean distance to a radially shifted Euclidean prototype; the core radial behavior mechanism survives without hyperbolic geometry, so curvature is not computationally necessary to the coupling. Operational switches are not fully specified.
EVIDENCE: BRANCH_RADIAL_FINE_CODES | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E12 E13 E14 E15
OBJECTION: BRANCH_RADIAL_FINE_CODES | The radial shift is collinear with each codeword, so it changes prototype magnitude rather than encoding a branch direction; the effect may be a generic norm-dependent preference, not preservation of branch-specific continuation distinctions.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: BRANCH_RADIAL_FINE_CODES | If all codewords have the same direction and residuals differ only in norm, then \(\rho_i\) changes prototype norms by entropy while no angular branch information is introduced; the same norm shift can be performed in Euclidean space.
RATIONALE: BRANCH_RADIAL_FINE_CODES | Measured successor branching statistics support the behavior signal (E5, E10). However, the curved distance over radially displaced prototypes has a direct Euclidean analogue, so geometry necessity is weak. The claimed assignment-to-recommendation path is plausible but does not specify a diagnostic that discriminates radial preference from branch preservation. The implementation is relatively concrete and data-derived, but the three controls are not specified operationally in the proposal. Novelty is UNKNOWN pending a bounded comparison with the mechanism ledger and cited work; exploration value is modest because the radial displacement has an obvious Euclidean counterpart.

SCORE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_FINE | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_FINE | IN_SCOPE | Directed training transitions choose a successor edge, and Poincaré geodesic codeword distances form a differentiable ranking loss at the final fine level, coupling behavior and geometry in codebook/encoder updates. The supplied proposal does not specify operational behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches.
EVIDENCE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_FINE | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E12 E13 E14 E15 E16
OBJECTION: TRANSITION_MARGIN_FINE | The ranking loss compares a source’s assigned codeword to the successor residual and can pull many successor residuals toward the same source codeword, collapsing distinctions rather than preserving successor-specific fine tokens.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_FINE | If two unrelated sources \(i_1,i_2\) have different assigned codewords but share successor \(j\), both losses can reduce by moving \(r_j\) toward both codewords; if those codewords are far apart, the objectives conflict and may instead distort assignments.
RATIONALE: TRANSITION_MARGIN_FINE | Train-only transition statistics are measured and support the behavior premise (E5, E10). Hyperbolic distance is explicit and differentiable, but no argument establishes added value against its matched Euclidean counterpart. The ranking gradient can alter fine-level residuals/codebooks and has a plausible route to successor predictability; the specific direction is uncertain because the pairwise objective may cause collapse or conflict. The proposal does not provide operational three-switch controls or a falsifier, despite a geometry sanity check in the bundle (E16). Novelty is UNKNOWN pending a bounded comparison with cited work and the ledger.

SCORE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FINE_BASIS | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=2 | novelty=UNKNOWN | downstream_mechanism=3 | falsifiability=2 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FINE_BASIS | IN_SCOPE | Training-only successor covariance defines an item-specific residual transform, and the transformed residual is quantized via Poincaré distance; behaviour and curvature jointly change the assignment computation. The proposal does not specify executable behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches.
EVIDENCE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FINE_BASIS | E1 E2 E3 E5 E10 E11 E12 E13 E14
OBJECTION: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FINE_BASIS | The specified shrinkage matrix can be singular or numerically unstable when the diagonal covariance is zero or tiny, and the proposed formula’s shrinkage factor is used both as an interpolation coefficient and inside the regularizer without clarifying the intended covariance shrinkage.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FINE_BASIS | For a deterministic successor profile, \(\Sigma_i=0\); if the global variance is also zero in any coordinate, the inverse square root has an infinite entry, so \(A_i r_i^3\) is undefined without an explicit positive floor.
RATIONALE: BRANCH_CONDITIONED_FINE_BASIS | Measured branch-degree and edge coverage support a real train-only behavior signal (E10–E11), while the proposal supplies a concrete covariance-derived frame and curved final assignment. Hyperbolic distance is explicit, but its advantage over the matched Euclidean whitening is not argued; the frame transform itself can be applied in Euclidean space. A path from successor covariance to changed fine assignments is plausible, with Stage3 impact still uncertain. The computation is implementable with diagonal covariance and precomputation, but requires explicit numerical floors and unambiguous shrinkage, plus operational switch definitions. Novelty is UNKNOWN because the bundle has no prior-art or ledger trace; a bounded comparison would resolve it.
